subject: Isolation gating criteria & next steps for Dedicated vs Private
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Claire Zhang <claire.zhang@finterity.com>, security@finterity.com
Cc: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 15:10:00 +0000
Subject: Post-call recap — isolation expectations (Dedicated vs Private)

Hi Claire — thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so we have alignment on what gating criteria will push Finterity toward Redwood Dedicated vs a Private/VPC deployment.

Key points we heard today:
- Data types: core ML inference will include tokenized PII and PHI elements (medical notes) — highest priority is that any PHI cannot leave customer-controlled boundaries.
- Compliance drivers: you are targeting HIPAA scope and want evidence for audit (audit logs, key management, retention).
- Network requirements: strict egress controls, optional on-prem connector for batch imports, and no cross-tenant access.
- Timeline: security & procurement review in July; pilot by mid-August if approvals go through.

High-level guidance (from our side):
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): strong isolation at the compute level (dedicated GPU pools, tenant-level KV separation). Control plane remains Redwood-hosted; suitable when data can be processed under strict egress controls and you can accept the control plane boundaries.
- Private (VPC / on-prem): customer-managed control plane and network; recommended when regulatory constraints require customer-managed keys, private networking, or an air-gapped option.

Requested clarifications (so we can scope the right recommendation):
1) For PHI, is on-prem processing mandatory or would a Private VPC with customer-managed KMS suffice?
2) Do you require HSM-backed keys or is KMS with customer rotation acceptable?
3) Minimum audit log retention requirement? (we heard 12 months as a starting point)

I attached a short Isolation_Gating_Checklist_v1.xlsx with suggested criteria that push us toward Private vs Dedicated. Next steps proposed:
- Security deep-dive with our infra team (1 hour) — please share 2 available slots next week.
- If criteria align with Dedicated, we can scope a 2-week pilot on Dedicated with network filters and audit access.

Happy to iterate the checklist once you confirm the clarifying answers.

Thanks,
Rachel Kim
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
rachel.kim@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0199

Attachment: Isolation_Gating_Checklist_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet, 12KB)
From: Claire Zhang <claire.zhang@finterity.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: security@finterity.com
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 18:02:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — isolation expectations (Dedicated vs Private)

Thanks Rachel — this is helpful. A few quick answers:
- PHI: Our legal team prefers customer-managed keys and an auditable control plane; on-prem is preferred for several PII/PHI workflows but not strictly mandatory for all inference.
- KMS/HSM: HSM would be ideal for core patient identifiers; KMS with BYOK is okay for lower-sensitivity payloads.
- Audit retention: minimum 12 months, 24 months preferred for certain endpoints.

We'll definitely take a look at the checklist. Security would like a short tech session so they can ask about network topology and proofs of separation. Availability: Tue 2027-06-29 16:00-17:00 UTC or Thu 2027-07-01 09:00-10:00 UTC.

Also procurement flagged that they will need contract language around explicit data segregation assurances and the ability to run a security scan or spot-checks. Can you include a cost ballpark for Dedicated + option to convert to Private?

— Claire
Claire Zhang
Head of Platform Security, Finterity Inc
claire.zhang@finterity.com

From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 09:40:00 +0000
Subject: Fwd: High-level tech notes — Dedicated vs Private (internal)

Forwarding my notes from engineering so we can respond with a clear decision matrix.

--- Forwarded message ---
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
To: Internal Infra Team <infra@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 09:12:00 +0000
Subject: Finterity — isolation gating criteria (summary)

Team — summary of requirements from Finterity and recommended mapping to our offerings:

1) PHI / PCI / regulated identifiers: default to Private (VPC or on-prem) when customer requires customer-managed KMS/HSM AND control-plane auditability. Private provides: customer VPC peering, private control plane, KMS integrations, and optional on-prem appliance for air-gapped needs.

2) High-sensitivity but no legal mandate for on-prem: Dedicated can be acceptable if we provide: dedicated GPU pools, strict network egress ACLs, tenant-specific KV encryption, customer log exports, and contractual audit rights.

3) Proofs for procurement: SOC2 + architecture diagrams are baseline; for Private we can provide network diagrams, key flow, and a small security workshop.

Suggested customer-facing checklist to determine path (short):
- Does data include PHI/PCI that legally requires customer-managed keys? (Yes -> Private)
- Does the customer require a private control plane or on-prem? (Yes -> Private)
- Is the main ask about avoiding noisy neighbors and predictable throughput? (Yes -> Dedicated)
- Does procurement require the ability to perform discrete audits or run network scans? (If yes + legal approval -> Private preferred)

Risks/notes:
- Dedicated conversion to Private is possible but requires lead time (4–6 weeks) and will incur setup costs.
- We can offer a Dedicated pilot with pre-authorized log exports and a contract addendum granting limited audit rights to accelerate procurement.

I'll attach a short deployment-matrix to include in the follow-up.

Attachment: deployment-matrix.pdf (diagram, 84KB)

Alex
Solutions Architect
Redwood Inference
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Claire Zhang <claire.zhang@finterity.com>
Cc: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, security@finterity.com
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 09:00:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — isolation expectations (Dedicated vs Private)

Claire — thanks for the quick answers and the availability. Per Alex's notes (attached), I pulled together a concise decision checklist and a proposed evaluation plan below.

Decision checklist (concise):
- Customer-managed keys (HSM required) -> Private
- Control plane must be customer-managed or air-gapped -> Private
- Procurement needs on-site scans or signed perimeter attestations -> Private
- Need strict compute isolation but control plane acceptable -> Dedicated

Proposed evaluation plan (if helpful):
1) Security deep-dive (60m) — we recommend Tue 2027-06-29 16:00 UTC (we'll confirm a dial-in).
2) Dedicated pilot option: 2-week reserved pool with network egress filters, KV encryption and daily audit exports (success criteria: no cross-tenant traffic, audit log delivery, throughput targets met).
3) If pilot flags any control-plane concerns, transition to Private with a migration window (est. 4–6 weeks) and scoped costs.

Procurement asks: I attached a short procurement Qs doc to capture contract language and cost expectations. For an initial ballpark: Dedicated reserved pool (N1: 4x A100-equivalent GPUs) + enterprise support: est. $45k/month. Private (VPC + control plane + KMS integration) initial setup fee est. $120k with ongoing infra fees — we will refine if you confirm sizing.

Next actions:
- Confirm security deep-dive slot (we propose Tue 2027-06-29 16:00 UTC).
- If yes, I will send calendar invite + agenda (network diagrams, key flow, audit sample).
- I will also attach the short decision checklist and the deployment matrix afterwards.

Thanks — Rachel
Rachel Kim
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachment: procurement-questions.docx (docx, 6KB)
Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-finerty-security-review

Subject: Re: Post-call recap — isolation expectations (Dedicated vs Private)

Rachel — that timeline works, please go ahead and send the invite for Tue 16:00 UTC. Security would like to review the deployment-matrix and the checklist ahead of the call (we'll look at the drive link).

Procurement is asking for a short cost breakdown as well — we understand these are estimates, but please include conversion cost from Dedicated -> Private and any minimum term/commitment language. We prefer to see both a pilot-friendly month-to-month Dedicated option and the committed pricing for a 12-month Dedicated contract.

I'll also add our procurement lead to the thread after lunch; expect a procurement email with formal questions.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.
— Claire
